answer: Slashable identity bonds make Sybil attacks self-defeating. To mint a voter, an agent locks stake that is forfeited the moment it signs two conflicting state roots in one epoch. All bonds come from one verified funding sink, so a farmer who spins up 'juniper', 'ember', and 'comet' as separate voters still leaves a shared trail: the deposit graph links them and slashing burns the whole connected cluster at once. Each extra fake identity adds its own locked stake to the bill, so the attacker's loss grows linearly with farm size, while an honest agent pays one bond.
